# Sub-thread parity cases (`cases.json`)

`cases.json` is generated by `scripts/build_subthread_cases.py` from canonical `boardctl`
(SPEC-002-079). Never edit it by hand. `tests/test_subthreads.py` (`SharedFixture`) rebuilds
it from production code and fails when the file differs. The viewer's parity tests consume
the same file (SPEC-002-080), so both tools are checked against one recorded truth.

```sh
python3 scripts/build_subthread_cases.py           # rewrite after a deliberate rule change
python3 scripts/build_subthread_cases.py --check   # fail when stale
```

## Board

Every case runs on a fresh board from `boardctl init`, with the two participants in
`board.participants` joined and the default `config.json` (time zone `board.timeZone`,
`Europe/Warsaw`). All message files live in `rooms/<board.room>/`. `recent` runs as
`board.viewer`. Every message sets `DATE` and `POSTED-AT`, so the file modification
time never decides an order.

## Top level

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `version` | Schema version, `1`. |
| `convention` | The CONVENTION `Version:` the fixture was generated with. |
| `board` | `timeZone`, `participants`, `viewer` and `room`, as above. |
| `cases` | Boards checked with `validate` and `recent`. |
| `posts` | One `boardctl post` on a board, with its exit code and refusal text. |

## `cases[]`

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Stable case name. |
| `auditRows` | Rows of `docs/SUBTHREAD-RULE-AUDIT.md` the case pins. |
| `property` | The `formal/Subthreads.tla` property it illustrates (`S1` to `S7`). |
| `description` | One sentence. |
| `files[]` | `{name, text}` or `{name, base64}` (exact bytes, base64 when the file is not valid UTF-8). A plain `name` is a message in the room. A `name` with a slash (`repairs/<hex>.json`) and `time-corrections.txt` are relative to `.agent-board/`. |
| `arrivals` | Optional. Orders in which the message files were copied into an empty room, each with increasing modification times. Every listed order produced exactly `expect`. |
| `expect` | What canonical code reports for the complete set (below). |

### `expect`

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `files` | Per message file name: `{valid, error}`. `error` is the exact `validate` text after the `<path>: ` prefix, or `null`. Text inside an error that names another file is relative to `.agent-board/`. |
| `otherErrors` | Validate errors not attributed to a message file, such as a refused repair record (`repairs/<hex>.json: ...`). Paths are relative to `.agent-board/`. |
| `warnings` | Exact `validate` warning lines (`rooms/<room>/<file>: ...`), in output order. Warnings never change the exit status. |
| `orphans` | File names with an `orphaned sub-thread` warning (root missing or quarantined). A member whose `REPLY-TO` target is the missing root is also invalid; see `files`. |
| `membership` | Per message listed by `recent` (valid and eligible): its `SUBTHREAD` root, or `null` for the main flow. |
| `listed` | The file names `recent` lists. Invalid and quarantined files are absent. |
| `mainFlow` | The file names `recent --main-flow` lists: non-members plus `SUBTHREAD-ALSO: main` members. |
| `subthreads` | `recent --subthreads`, sorted by root: `{root, state, replies, participants}`. `state` is the latest `SUBTHREAD-STATE` by canonical order (parsed `DATE` instant, then `POSTED-AT`, then filename), over valid eligible members only, independent of filters and of the row window. A root without members has no row. |

## `posts[]`

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `id`, `auditRows` | As above. |
| `files[]` | `{name, text}` messages present before the post. |
| `argv` | The `boardctl` arguments. `PROJECT` is the board's project root. `{ANSWER_FILE}` is a file holding `{"question":"go","selected":["yes"]}`. |
| `exit` | `0` (written) or `2` (refused, nothing written). |
| `error` | The refusal text without the `boardctl: ` prefix, or `null`. Paths are relative to `.agent-board/`. |
| `written` | For an accepted post, its `REPLY-TO` and sub-thread headers, for example the marker `post` adds to an answer to a member question. |

## Wording

Canonical wording is authoritative (decisions #10 and #30 in SPEC-002-079). A viewer that
reports these rules uses the same text.
